# mbse-programs

> Programs as language-neutral data: complete abstract syntax trees, built on mbse-schemas, that a transpiler builds, reads and rewrites in memory without parsing or printing strings. Each language's kinds cover the union of its standards and record which standard has each construct; standards parse source text into trees through an established parser and print trees back. The languages are Ccpp (C and C++: kinds for C++26 and C23, with C++17 and C++20 parsed by tree-sitter-cpp), Python (kinds following Python's `ast` through 3.15, with Python 3.12 and 3.14 parsed by tree-sitter-python, checked against CPython) and TypeScript (TypeScript and JavaScript: kinds following typescript-estree through TypeScript 5.9 and ES2025, with JSX, parsed by tree-sitter-typescript, checked against typescript-estree) and Verilog (Verilog and SystemVerilog: kinds for SystemVerilog 2023's design subset and verification constructs, with Verilog-2005 and SystemVerilog 2017 and 2023 read by slang, which TypeScript runs through the Python implementation). A transpiler translates a subset of TypeScript into Python, tree to tree, and a bridge carries expressions between mbse-expressions' Python dialect and Python's trees. Equivalent Python (`mbse.Programs`) and TypeScript (`@mbse/programs`) implementations give the same trees and byte-identical JSON.

Trees are plain mutable objects with typed properties; every kind has an mbse-schemas meta-schema, so trees serialize as JSON or YAML. `Definitions` gives the entities a program declares and resolves names from where they are written.

## Why

- [MBSE.md](https://github.com/pitaman71/mbse-programs/blob/main/MBSE.md): executable specifications, and each mbse repository's part in them

## Learning it

- [Python tutorial](https://github.com/pitaman71/mbse-programs/blob/main/python3/tutorials/README.md) and [TypeScript tutorial](https://github.com/pitaman71/mbse-programs/blob/main/typescript5/tutorials/README.md): eight case studies, from code as text to code generated from the rules of an executable specification

## Using it

- [Agent skill](https://github.com/pitaman71/mbse-programs/blob/main/skills/mbse-programs/SKILL.md): when to use it, the rules that prevent most mistakes, and references loaded per task
- [Python](https://github.com/pitaman71/mbse-programs/blob/main/skills/mbse-programs/references/python.md) and [TypeScript](https://github.com/pitaman71/mbse-programs/blob/main/skills/mbse-programs/references/typescript.md): a complete program, cheat sheet and traps
- [Languages](https://github.com/pitaman71/mbse-programs/blob/main/skills/mbse-programs/references/languages.md) and [transpiling](https://github.com/pitaman71/mbse-programs/blob/main/skills/mbse-programs/references/transpiling.md): each language's kinds, standards and gaps; rewriting, transpilers and bridges
- [README](https://github.com/pitaman71/mbse-programs/blob/main/README.md): a complete example in each language
- [PROGRAMS.md](https://github.com/pitaman71/mbse-programs/blob/main/docs/PROGRAMS.md): trees, standards, Ccpp, Python and TypeScript, parsing and its known gaps, printing, definitions, transpiling, bridges, and open questions
